item.title: Four Chinese sites added to World Heritage Irrigation Structures list
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Four Chinese sites added to World Heritage Irrigation Structures list BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Four Chinese irrigation projects have been added to the World Heritage Irrigation Structures (WHIS) list, bringing the country's total to 46, the Ministry of Water Resources said Thursday. The projects, located in Henan, Gansu, Jiangxi and Fujian provinces, were recognized during the 77th International Executive Council Meeting of the International Commission on Irrigation and Drainage (ICID) in Marseille, France, on Wednesday. Dating back more than 2,200 years, a canal irrigation system in central China's Henan Province uses dam-free water diversion to irrigate about 34,000 hectares of farmland in Jiyuan and Jiaozuo. The irrigated farmland forms a major grain-producing area in the province. In northwest China's Gansu Province, an oasis irrigation system in the Hexi Corridor, a key artery of the ancient Silk Road, dates back to the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644). It irrigates about 63,200 hectares of land and is a typical example of oasis irrigation in arid regions of Eurasia. The project in Shangrao City, east China's Jiangxi Province, dates back to the Song Dynasty (960-1279). Its gravity-fed irrigation network consists of canals, weirs and ponds. Another ancient irrigation system in Changtai District of Zhangzhou City, southeast China's Fujian Province, has a history of more than 800 years. Featuring low dams and a network of weirs, ponds and canals, it irrigates about 1,850 hectares of land. China has a long history of irrigation engineering. The Dujiangyan irrigation system in southwest China's Sichuan Province, built in 256 BC, remains in use today and was added to the WHIS list in 2018. Established by the ICID in 2014, the WHIS designation aims to protect and promote irrigation projects of historical value and scientific experience. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Tech innovations take spotlight at Canton Fair
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Tech innovations take spotlight at Canton Fair A visitor checks out a motorbike during the Canton Fair in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, on Thursday. WANG ZHUANGFEI/CHINA DAILY Inside the Pazhou Complex, Leaw Cheeeyrn, a Malaysian businessman with high-level paraplegia, was able to walk with the assistance of a robotic exoskeletal device. "It was wonderful and I hope there will be more such high-tech products to help us walk," he said. He was accompanied by his wife at the China Import and Export Fair, which opened its 140th session in Guangzhou, capital of Guangdong province, on Thursday. At the event — also widely known as the Canton Fair — domestically produced high-tech products, especially artificial intelligence-driven electronic products and medical equipment, were highly favored by foreign buyers. The fair aligns with new trends in foreign trade, with 64 percent of the 32,000 participating companies utilizing new technologies such as AI and industrial internet, according to the organizers. The proportion of new and green products exhibited reached 23.2 percent and 26 percent, respectively, both setting records, the organizers said. China's manufacturing sector has been continuously transforming and upgrading, leading to an optimized foreign trade structure and a steady increase in the technological content of import and export products. Electronic components, industrial robots, 3D printers and new energy vehicles have performed exceptionally well, becoming new drivers of foreign trade momentum, the organizers said. "We are very interested in selling these products to Malaysia, where there will be high demand for intelligent robotic products," the Malaysian businessman said. The exoskeleton robotic device, developed by RoboCT — a Chinese company dedicated to the development and application of exoskeleton robotics — has been sold to more than 50 countries and regions. "We have developed intelligent products that help people with walking disabilities walk again and better," said Zhang Jiyu, co-founder and chief operating officer of RoboCT. On the fair's opening day, the company's exhibition booth attracted a large number of foreign buyers from the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Europe, Japan and South Korea. The company displayed its new rehabilitation service of mind-driven exoskeletons powered by brainwave signals and its GoGo-H Pro climbing series — a consumer-grade assistive exoskeleton for daily mobility. "We have brought a comprehensive product lineup covering medical rehabilitation, daily mobility assistance and industry support, aiming to showcase to our global partners the full-spectrum application capabilities of Chinese exoskeleton technology," Zhang said. The company, based in Hangzhou, capital of Zhejiang province, realized a year-on-year increase of 46.22 percent in overseas sales in 2025. In the first eight months of this year, its overseas sales increased about 149.76 percent year-on-year. At the fair's 139th session in April, the company — participating for the first time — successfully obtained the contact information of over 40 overseas distributors, with the total value of intended orders exceeding $3.5 million. "The fair is an important window for Chinese manufacturers to reach the world and a key milestone in our globalization strategy," said Zhang. The fair, seen as a barometer of China's foreign trade, runs in three phases from Oct 15 to Nov 4. Over the past 70 years, the fair has grown into China's largest and longest-running international trade event, with the most complete product range, the largest number of buyers and the highest transaction volume. item.title: Chinese sand-control pioneer Yin Yuzhen named among FAO's 100 women heroes
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Chinese sand-control pioneer Yin Yuzhen named among FAO's 100 women heroes Yin Yuzhen attends a ceremony for Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations' (FAO) 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development, in Rome, Italy, Oct. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Kaiyan) FAO Director-General Qu Dongyu said women are a driving force in agrifood systems, playing an indispensable role in food security, natural resource management, rural development and community resilience. ROME, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Chinese sand-control pioneer Yin Yuzhen has been named among the FAO's 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development, a global recognition initiative launched by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). The honorees were celebrated at a ceremony on Thursday at the FAO headquarters in Rome as part of this year's World Food Forum. Yin has spent more than four decades combating desertification in the Maowusu Sandy Land in north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. After decades of persistent tree planting, she and her family have transformed stretches of the once-barren landscape into a green expanse, overcoming harsh conditions and shifting sands. Her story also forged an enduring friendship with retired U.S. teacher Ronald Sakolsky, who raised 5,000 U.S. dollars decades ago to support her afforestation work. Yin told Xinhua that the recognition had strengthened her resolve to continue her work. "Like a Mongolian horse, I will keep pressing forward with perseverance and determination, doing my work well and giving back to nature," she said. Chinese sand-control pioneer Yin Yuzhen (2nd L, front) attends a ceremony in Rome, Italy, Oct. 15, 2026. Chinese sand-control pioneer Yin Yuzhen was named on Thursday among the FAO's 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development, a global recognition initiative launched by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). (Xinhua/Li Jing) Sitting in the audience, Sakolsky's eyes grew moist as he applauded Yin's achievement. "Yin deserves everything that she gets. She is the heroine," he told Xinhua. Addressing the ceremony, FAO Director-General Qu Dongyu hailed women farmers' roles. He said women are a driving force in agrifood systems, playing an indispensable role in food security, natural resource management, rural development and community resilience. Qu then invited Sakolsky to join Yin on stage. The two friends embraced once again and held up a trophy together. Qu said that although Sakolsky was not among the women heroes, his "passion" and "solidarity" should be recognized. Sakolsky expressed his gratitude, saying he was deeply moved by Yin's remarkable achievement. He called on everyone to plant a tree and work together to make a difference to the environment. Director-General of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) Qu Dongyu (L) presents the award to Dong Minfang during a ceremony for FAO's 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development, in Rome, Italy, Oct. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Kaiyan) Launched by the FAO to mark the International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026, the global initiative recognizes 100 women for their outstanding contributions to agriculture, food systems and rural development. The FAO said it received 609 nominations from 131 members. The selection process involved an eligibility review, an assessment, and ranking by senior management, and two rounds of deliberations. Besides Yin, Yu Jinxiu and Dong Minfang were also among the FAO 100 Women Heroes. Yu is a moxibustion therapist from Qichun County in central China's Hubei Province, and Dong is president of the Fengrui Agricultural Machinery Professional Cooperative in Yueyang County, central China's Hunan Province. They have spent years sharing their expertise to help thousands of people secure jobs and start businesses, raising incomes for rural residents. The United Nations designated 2026 as the International Year of the Woman Farmer to highlight women's contribution to agrifood systems and promote policies and investments that improve their access to finance, knowledge and services. Director-General of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) Qu Dongyu (L) presents the award to Yu Jinxiu during a ceremony for FAO's 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development, in Rome, Italy, Oct. 15, 2026. item.title: China's FDI equity stock ranks second globally: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
China's FDI equity stock ranks second globally: commerce ministry BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign direct investment (FDI) equity stock reached 26.8 trillion yuan (about 3.98 trillion U.S. dollars) in 2025, ranking second globally and marking six consecutive years of growth, the Ministry of Commerce said Thursday, citing the latest annual reports from foreign-invested enterprises. A total of 461,000 foreign-invested enterprises filed annual reports last year, up 5.7 percent from 2024, according to data compiled by the ministry and other government departments. China's vast market offers foreign businesses opportunities to generate tangible returns, ministry spokesperson He Yadong told a press conference, adding that China welcomes foreign companies seeking to expand their presence in the country and share in its development opportunities. The reporting companies posted an average profit margin of 8.7 percent in 2025. In the manufacturing sector, their profit margin was 2.2 percentage points higher than that of China's major industrial enterprises, the data showed. Foreign-invested enterprises accounted for one-third of China's total goods trade and one-seventh of the country's tax revenue in 2025. They also provided an average of more than 30 million jobs annually over the past five years, the ministry said. High-tech industries have become a bright spot for foreign investment in China. FDI in the sector rose 35.1 percent year on year to 200.26 billion yuan in the first eight months of this year, official data showed. China has stepped up efforts to stabilize foreign investment and direct more capital into advanced and high-value-added sectors. A 15-measure action plan unveiled in June this year aims to expand market access, streamline investment procedures, strengthen investment promotion and improve services for foreign investors. A new version of the Catalog of Encouraged Industries for Foreign Investment also took effect on Feb. 1, encouraging foreign investment in advanced manufacturing, modern services, high-tech industries, energy conservation and environmental protection, as well as in China's central, western and northeastern regions. item.title: Beijing forum discusses counter-terrorism challenges posed by intelligent technologies
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Beijing forum discusses counter-terrorism challenges posed by intelligent technologies Participants communicate with each other during the Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 14, 2026. The Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism concluded here on Thursday. (Photo by Yue Chang/Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism concluded in Beijing on Thursday, with more than 320 experts and frontline personnel from 62 countries and international organizations discussing counter-terrorism challenges, including those arising from advances in unmanned and intelligent technologies. During the three-day forum, participants discussed the terrorism situation, explored solutions to common challenges, exchanged practical experience and explored avenues for international cooperation. Participants noted that the rapid development of unmanned and intelligent technologies has made terrorist activities increasingly covert and destructive, as new methods are adopted to carry out acts of terrorism and violence. They said traditional approaches that rely on individual countries acting alone and isolated prevention and control measures are increasingly inadequate to address emerging terrorist threats that are transnational, covert and enabled by intelligent technologies. The participants said combating terrorism requires countries to keep pace with advances in unmanned and intelligent technologies, strengthen their counter-terrorism capabilities, and work together to establish and improve international cooperation mechanisms for preventing and combating terrorism. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the Great Wall forum. Since its launch in 2016, the Chinese People's Armed Police Force has hosted six editions of the forum. This year's event focused on changing circumstances, evolving adversaries and technological advances, and examined the impact of artificial intelligence on efforts to prevent and combat terrorism. Discussions were organized into high-level, professional and thematic forums, creating a comprehensive, multilevel dialogue platform spanning the strategic, operational and tactical levels. An important participant in and contributor to the global fight against terrorism, China has engaged in pragmatic cooperation with other countries in terms of intelligence exchanges, border control, case investigations and counter-terrorism financing. It has also organized training sessions and seminars to share its experience with the international community and help strengthen counter-terrorism capabilities. item.title: Long March legacy takes root in greener landscapes of revolutionary heartlands
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Long March legacy takes root in greener landscapes of revolutionary heartlands This aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 4, 2026 shows a general view of Zhongfu Village in Changting County, southeast China's Fujian Province. (Photo by Zhu Fangbin/Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Perched on a hillside in Changting County of southern China, visitors soak in lush scenery stretching beside the glistening Tingjiang River. But things weren't always so picturesque. Changting, an old revolutionary base area in Fujian Province, was among the counties hardest hit by soil erosion in China's red-soil region, which threatened local people's livelihoods and left the landscape degraded. Efforts to improve the local environment began nearly a century ago. In November 1931, the Communist Party of China (CPC) established the Provisional Central Government of the Chinese Soviet Republic in Ruijin, Jiangxi Province, where the CPC put its revolutionary ideals into governance experimentation. The following year, it launched a tree-planting campaign to protect farmland from floods and droughts, reclaim barren hills and benefit local people. During this campaign, CPC-led Red Army soldiers in Changting, which neighbors Ruijin, taught residents how to plant trees. In turn, residents brought food and seedlings to the soldiers and joined the planting campaign voluntarily. "Even amid the turmoil of war, the Party still called for tree planting with great vigor," said Chen Liping, a researcher of CPC history and local chronicles in the county. "It reflects the Party's commitment to putting people's interests first and laying the foundations for future development." As the war intensified, however, the tree-planting campaign had to be halted. The Red Army then embarked on the Long March, an epic military trek from 1934 to 1936 that broke through the encirclement of Kuomintang (Nationalist Party) forces. With some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers, the arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. As one of the starting points of the Long March, Changting has carried forward the Red Army's legacy in its decades-long efforts to combat soil erosion. Tree planting, as the Red Army had practiced earlier, remained an effective method to tackle the problem. However, in severely eroded areas, ground temperatures can soar above 70 degrees Celsius, making it difficult for trees to survive. Through experimentation, the county developed a phased approach suited to its natural conditions: first planting grass, then shrubs, and next trees, bringing the barren hills back to life step by step. "Grass helps lower ground temperatures and create favorable conditions for other vegetation, allowing a mix of tree species to take root," said Shangguan Yuanbin, deputy head of the county's soil and water conservation station. Over the years, local people adapted to changing conditions and met emerging problems with determination, patience and ingenuity. Years of effort have paid off. To date, Changting has reduced the area affected by soil erosion by about 1.17 million mu (about 78,000 hectares), while its soil erosion rate fell from 31.47 percent to 6.31 percent, according to local authorities. "Had we given up at any point over these decades, we would not have achieved such results today," said Shangguan. "We've applied the fearless Long March spirit to soil and water conservation." Changting's transformation epitomizes a broader greening trend in China, which marks a national tree-planting day annually. Official data showed that between 2021 and 2025, China accounted for roughly one-quarter of the world's increase in green vegetation, while its forest and grass coverage rate exceeded 56 percent in 2025. China's greening endeavor has gained international recognition. In 2021, Changting's comprehensive soil erosion control and ecological restoration practices were selected as a model case at the 15th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP15). But restoring the land is not the end of the story. The next challenge is to turn environmental recovery into lasting economic opportunities for local communities. One of these places is Xikuangshan, an old mining area in central China's Hunan Province. During the Long March, about 1,500 well-disciplined Red Army soldiers were stationed there for a week. Through their words and deeds, they gained the trust of locals, who went from hiding from the Red Army to following it. Dubbed the "World's Capital of Antimony," Xikuangshan has witnessed decades of intensive underground mining dating back to 1897, which led to vegetation loss, air and water pollution, and ground subsidence. Some even joked that "a white bird flying across Xikuangshan could turn black." In 2004, local people mounted an all-out campaign for ecological restoration. Inspired by the perseverance shown by the Red Army, a research team conducted countless experiments and finally achieved a breakthrough in the treatment of harmful residue generated during antimony refining, a challenge that has long confronted the industry worldwide. The once-scarred mining landscape gradually regained its vitality. The improved environment, together with its revolutionary history and mining culture, helped Xikuangshan to develop into a well-known tourist destination with around 300 million yuan (about 44.6 million U.S. dollars) in tourism revenue annually. Yang Lijun is among those who have benefited. After more than a decade, he decided to return home in 2021 upon seeing his hometown's blue skies and clear waters. He rented an abandoned rural house and opened a tourist restaurant featuring local specialties, which now generates an annual income of more than 100,000 yuan. "In the past, many residents, myself included, left home because of worsening environmental conditions," he recalled. "Now, with the environment improving, more tourists are coming, bringing new opportunities for a better life." For places like Changting and Xikuangshan, ecological restoration is therefore not simply about bringing back greenery, but also about higher-quality lives and new development paths for former revolutionary base areas. Earlier this year, China issued guidelines on accelerating the development of such areas, with measures to support systematic environmental protection and encourage eco-tourism. For Yue Hui, director of the soil and water conservation center in Changting, the changes are encouraging, but the work is far from over. "Combating soil erosion requires sustained effort. We will continue our march toward a greener future," Yue said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

Xi congratulates Hunan University on its centenary BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday extended congratulations to faculty, students and alumni of Hunan University as it marks its 100th anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a congratulatory letter to the university. Xi urged the university to carry forward fine revolutionary traditions, continue to elevate the quality and levels of its teaching, and strive to nurture more talent who can apply their knowledge to practical affairs, so as to make new contributions to building China into an education powerhouse and advancing Chinese modernization. Founded in 1926, Hunan University has nurtured a wealth of outstanding talent over the past century. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
